content.value_statement: Flutter teams must handle architecture, performance, testing, and deployment across platforms. This skill provides structured guidance for Dart 3, Flutter 3, state management, UI, security, and release workflows.
actual_capabilities: Recommends Flutter architecture patterns, including clean architecture, MVVM, feature modules, repositories, and dependency injection.
Compares state management choices such as Riverpod, Bloc, Provider, GetX, MobX, Redux, and custom approaches.
Guides widget composition, custom rendering, animations, accessibility, responsive layouts, and design system work.
Supports performance planning for rebuild reduction, memory profiling, image caching, large lists, isolates, and frame rendering.
Outlines testing strategies for unit, widget, golden, integration, performance, accessibility, CI, and device farm testing.
Covers platform integration, deployment, signing, store compliance, secure storage, authentication, and privacy considerations.
limitations: Does not execute Flutter commands, inspect projects, or validate builds unless the host agent has those tools.
May reference ecosystem versions from the skill text, so verify current package APIs before release.
Cannot replace hands-on testing across real devices, stores, browsers, and accessibility tools.
Requires clear product goals, target platforms, and constraints for precise recommendations.

use_cases.title: Plan A Cross-Platform App
use_cases.description: Define architecture, state management, and platform boundaries before implementation starts.

use_cases.title: Improve Existing Flutter Code
use_cases.description: Identify performance, accessibility, testing, and architecture changes for a mature codebase.

use_cases.title: Prepare A Store Release
use_cases.description: Create checklists for signing, compliance, monitoring, testing, and deployment across app stores.

prompt_templates.title: Plan My First Feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a Flutter feature for [app type]. Include widget structure, state management, loading states, error handling, accessibility, and tests.

prompt_templates.title: Choose State Management
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare Riverpod, Bloc, Provider, and GetX for [project]. Recommend one option and explain migration impact, testing approach, and risks.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize A Slow Screen
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Flutter screen description: [details]. Identify rebuild, layout, image, memory, and networking bottlenecks. Suggest measurable fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Architect Multi-Platform Delivery
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Flutter architecture for [product] across iOS, Android, web, and desktop. Include modules, platform channels, CI, security, monitoring, and release gates.

output_examples.input: I need to build an offline-first task app in Flutter.
output: Recommends clean architecture with repositories and local persistence.
Suggests Riverpod or Bloc for predictable state and testability.
Lists sync conflicts, loading states, accessibility checks, and release validation steps.

output_examples.input: My Flutter list screen drops frames during scrolling.
output: Focuses on rebuild profiling, const widgets, stable keys, and item virtualization.
Advises image caching, pagination, and isolates for heavy work.
Defines measurements with DevTools frame timing and real-device benchmarks.

output_examples.input: We need native camera features in a Flutter app.
output: Explains platform channels, plugin boundaries, permissions, and fallback behavior.
Adds testing needs for iOS and Android devices.
Includes privacy, error handling, and store review considerations.

best_practices: Share target platforms, app size, performance goals, and release constraints before asking for architecture guidance.
Ask for tests, accessibility checks, and failure states with every implementation plan.
Validate package choices, store rules, and platform APIs against current documentation before shipping.
anti_patterns: Do not request generic Flutter advice without product goals, platform targets, or existing constraints.
Do not treat generated architecture as final without profiling, tests, and device validation.
Do not mix many state management frameworks unless there is a clear migration or boundary plan.

faq.question: What kind of Flutter work does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports architecture, widgets, state management, testing, performance, platform integration, deployment, and security planning.

faq.question: Does it write complete applications?
faq.answer: It can guide implementation plans and code structure, but full apps still need project-specific development and testing.

faq.question: Can it help choose Riverpod, Bloc, Provider, or GetX?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide app complexity, team experience, testing needs, and migration constraints for a useful recommendation.

faq.question: Does it cover Flutter web and desktop?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes responsive design, platform integration, deployment, and performance considerations for web and desktop targets.

faq.question: Can it validate my build or run tests?
faq.answer: Only when the host agent has access to your project files and local Flutter tooling.

faq.question: Is it suitable for production release planning?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers signing, CI, monitoring, app store requirements, privacy, testing, and deployment workflows.
